items.stem: A common mistake in finance transformation is to:

options.text: Automate a broken process instead of standardising and fixing it first
options.rationale: Correct: automating waste entrenches it; standardise first.
Standardising first is the recommended approach, not a mistake.
Clear SLAs are good practice, not a mistake.

items.stem: Which TWO are typical goals of moving finance work into a shared-service centre? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Standardised, consistent processing across the organisation
options.rationale: Correct: shared services drive standardisation and consistency.

options.text: Lower unit cost through scale and efficiency
options.rationale: Correct: scale and efficiency reduce processing cost.

options.text: Letting every local office invent its own process
options.rationale: Shared services reduce, not increase, local variation.
Shared services rely on SLAs and metrics.

items.explanation: Correct: shared services drive standardisation and consistency.

items.stem: Good shared-service metrics focus primarily on:

options.text: Service outcomes and quality, not just activity volume
options.rationale: Correct: outcome and quality metrics reflect real performance.

options.text: Only the number of transactions processed
options.rationale: Volume alone is a vanity metric missing quality.
Headcount cuts are not a service-quality metric.
Targets and SLAs are essential to shared services.
